name: dlt_transactions
description: What the DLT connector sent to the Hiero network and what came back. One row per attempt to anchor a transaction, a user registration or a transaction link on the chain.
source: database/src/entity/DltTransaction.ts and database/src/schemas/drizzle.schema.ts plus database/migration/migrations 0070, 0101 and 0103

columns.name: type_id
columns.description: Which of the three reference columns is the meaningful one.

columns.name: hiero_transaction_id
columns.description: The network's own identifier for the submitted transaction. NULL until it has been sent.

columns.name: verified
columns.description: Whether the network confirmed it. Redundant with verified_at — see the note.

columns.name: error
columns.description: Why the network rejected it. Set by the rejectedTx notification, see server/federation/blockchain-notification.json.

unique.name: dlt_transactions_hiero_transacion_id_unique
unique.note: The name is misspelled in legacy ('transacion'). Names are stable forever — see contracts/AGENTS.md — so it is written here as it is, not as it should have been.

notes: verified and verified_at say the same thing twice, and nothing in the schema keeps them in step. Both implementations must write both or gradido2 must drop the boolean; a row with verified = true and verified_at NULL is an inconsistency, not a state.
The unique on hiero_transaction_id is what makes the confirmation idempotent: the same notification arriving twice cannot create a second row. It is a correctness constraint, not an optimisation.
error set together with verified = true is a contradiction. A row is confirmed or rejected, never both — the same rule contributions.json states for confirmed_by and denied_by.
Timestamps are UTC milliseconds; see types/Timestamp.json. This table uses datetime(3).
